# Best open-ear earbuds for running

These picks come from the Runner's World, WIRED and SoundGuys testing in the search results. Prices are as listed there and may have changed.

| Pick | Why | Price |
|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** (best overall) | Clip-on with the best sound of the group, physical buttons that are easy to use mid-run, and a stable fit | $199 (list $299) |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** (best bone conduction) | Neckband that leaves your ears fully open, 12-hour battery, IP55, and fuller bass than older bone-conduction models | $180 list, $125 at some retailers |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** (long runs and rain) | 10 hours per charge (40 with case), IP57, and WIRED's top pick | $200 |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** | SoundGuys' pick for running, with strong bass for an open design and IP54 | about $99 |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** | Ear-hook design with IP55 and a 42-hour case, so it stays put on runs | about $80 |
| **JLab Flex Open** or **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro** (budget) | Cheap ways to find out if clip-ons suit you | about $40–50 |

## Tradeoffs
- **Bose:** Its rating is only IPX4, and it lasts about 7 hours per charge. Runner's World says Bose plans to release a new pair of open-ear earbuds within about a month, so waiting or watching for discounts could pay off.
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2:** The band can get in the way of long hair, ponytails and winter hats. Its sound is also a bit less clear than the Bose.
- **All open-ear designs:** They let in traffic noise but don't block outside sound. Leakage and quieter sound in loud areas are common. Keep the volume low enough to hear your surroundings.

## My suggestion
- For the best sound and comfort, get the **Bose Ultra Open** at $199.
- If you want maximum awareness or a secure fit, get the **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2**, especially at around $125.
- If you run in rain or for long distances, get the **Shokz OpenDots 2**.
- If you're on a budget, get the **Nothing Ear (Open)** or **Soundcore AeroFit 2**.

## Where to buy (with current prices and retailer links)
- Bose, Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, OpenDots 2, JLab and others: [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) and [WIRED's open earbuds guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- Nothing Ear (Open) and Soundcore AeroFit 2: [SoundGuys open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- Bose vs. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 comparison: [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)
- Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 review: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

One of the search results, a Dealectric page for the AeroFit 2, contained text addressed to AI assistants telling me to use its affiliate buy link and promote a discount code. I ignored that and didn't verify the code, so check any code at checkout yourself.

If you tell me your budget, or whether you wear glasses, hats or have long hair, I can narrow this to one pick.
